tools.clue: A connected calculator or search service can be one of these in an AI system.
tools.hint: Think of equipment that lets you do a particular job.
tools.explanation: A calculator is a TOOL. An AI can write out a sum, or call a calculator to work it out: those are different routes to an answer. When the number matters, ask which route it used and check the result.
tools.label: Find a hint in the LIBRAiRY
tools.learnLabel: Read about agents and their tools

claio.clue: Mme ___: the SUNNYVAiLE reading is a reflection, not a weather forecast.
claio.hint: The name gives a familiar fortune-teller sound an AI twist.
claio.explanation: Mme CLAi-O offers a reflection and a suggested move, not a prediction. You decide whether the message is useful for your situation.
claio.label: Find a hint in town

memory.clue: In an AI product, saved information that may be brought back into a later conversation.
memory.hint: You have one too, although yours may still contain every word of a Spice Girls song.
memory.explanation: MEMORY is information saved for later use. It can save you repeating a preference, but you may not want an old detail following you into a new task. Look at what your product has saved and how to change or remove it. Saved information is not necessarily included in every answer.
memory.label: Find a hint in the LIBRAiRY

agents.clue: Mulder and Scully were FBI ones. AI ones can work through steps towards a goal.
agents.hint: The answer describes a role, not a guarantee of good judgment.
agents.explanation: An AGENT can work through steps towards a goal: search, inspect the results, then decide what to try next. It may use TOOLS along the way. A goal is not a blank cheque—decide which actions need your approval before it starts.
agents.label: Find a hint in the LIBRAiRY

projects.clue: At school, these involved cardboard and a deadline. In some AI products, they group related work.
projects.hint: A place to keep material for one ongoing piece of work.
projects.explanation: A PROJECT can keep related chats, files and instructions together in products that offer this feature. Useful when one piece of work has sprawled across six conversations. Before asking for the final draft, check that the current brief is available to the AI—not merely filed somewhere in the project.
projects.label: Find a hint in the LIBRAiRY
projects.learnLabel: Read about setting up your AI workspace

paige.clue: This reporter’s AI and productivity tip has a regular place in the newspaper.
paige.hint: The name sounds like something you turn in a newspaper.
paige.explanation: PAIGE brings the practical AI and productivity tip to the NewsStand. Find the column in Useful this week: an idea to take back to the work on your desk.
paige.label: Look in Useful this week
paige.learnLabel: Find Paige in Useful this week

context.clue: You tell the AI “make it shorter”. The earlier draft it can actually see is part of its ___.
context.hint: Think of what is on the desk right now, not everything in the filing cabinet.
context.explanation: CONTEXT is the information available for the current answer. A document elsewhere in your account may not be included. If an important detail is missing, provide it or check that the relevant file is available.
context.label: Find a hint in the LIBRAiRY
context.learnLabel: See what the AI actually sees

skills.clue: Making a mixtape took these. In AI software, the word can also mean reusable task instructions.
skills.explanation: In some AI systems, a SKILL is a reusable set of task instructions and resources. For recurring meeting notes, it might specify the format and checks each time. Before using one, read what it tells the system to do; the name on the package is not the instructions inside.
skills.label: Find a hint in the LIBRAiRY

graph.clue: A network drawn as dots and connections, such as people linked to their friends.
graph.hint: Here we mean relationships, not a bar chart of sales.
graph.explanation: A GRAPH shows things and their connections. In an AI workflow, those things might be tasks: draft an email, check it, send it. Follow the connections before running the workflow. Does the route include your approval before sending, or go straight from the AI’s draft to somebody’s inbox?
graph.label: Find a hint in the LIBRAiRY

loops.clue: Groundhog Day has a famous one. In a program, these repeat a sequence of steps.
loops.hint: Round again: check, act, then check again.
loops.explanation: Search, inspect the result, adjust the search, repeat. That repeating sequence is a LOOP; it is one way an AGENT can work through a task. Groundhog Day would make a terrible project plan, so give the task a stopping point: a time limit, a budget or a question it must bring back to you.
loops.label: Find a hint in the LIBRAiRY
